evidence.field: Oracle-bone and bronze records; editorial explanation
evidence.text: The page lists oracle-bone example 合集19050 and bronze example 集成02836. Its analysis describes 天 as a frontal standing human figure with the head emphasized, and says the head mark was later reduced to a horizontal stroke. It proposes extension from head to the sky above.
evidence.title: 漢字「天」：字形演變

evidence.source: 考古資料數位典藏創新計畫, Academia Sinica
evidence.text: The account identifies 大 as the frontal standing-person basis and the mark above it as the person’s head, later often simplified to a horizontal stroke. This is an institutional explanatory analysis, not a direct transcription of a dated inscription.
evidence.title: 甲骨文 中與「天」相關的字

search_audit.outcome: Opened and inspected the 天 form-history page and the institutional explanation. The 天 page supplies oracle-bone and bronze identifiers and interprets 大 as the human figure basis with an emphasized head mark.

gaps: The direct Commons SVG could not be opened by the web tool, so its rendered strokes were not visually inspected here. Its identity, Shang-style description, Xiaoxuetang exemplar reference, and CC0 status are established by the exact Commons description page.

The cited paleographic interpretation supports 大 as the graphic basis for the person and the upper mark as emphasized head, but does not establish a certain earliest spoken meaning or resolve the disputed head/top-to-sky semantic chronology.

items.period: Shang-style oracle script; modern vector redraw of a Xiaoxuetang exemplar identified as image 41.E045
items.caption: This modern redraw presents 天 in Shang oracle-script style. Paleographers interpret the graph as a standing person based on 大, with the upper mark emphasizing the head; this interpretation does not settle whether head/top or sky was the word’s earlier meaning.
items.alt: Modern vector redraw of a Shang-style oracle-script form of 天, with a marked upper stroke above a human-like figure.
items.selection_reason: The exact Commons page verifies the file’s identity, Shang-style label, Xiaoxuetang source exemplar, and reuse status. The form is relevant to the cited head-marked analysis; its picture itself was not visually inspected during research.
items.rights: CC0 1.0 as stated on the Commons description page; the page attributes the exemplar image to Xiaoxuetang.

limitations.text: The image is a modern redraw, not an ancient artifact photograph. The original SVG link was identified on its Commons description page but failed to open directly in this session, so the image was not visually inspected.
The human-figure and marked-head account is a paleographic interpretation; it does not determine the earliest spoken sense of 天 or prove a complete semantic development from head/top to sky/heaven.
